name: Realtime voice conversation (OpenAI realtime or GPT-Live over WebRTC)
description: Low-latency, interruptible speech-to-speech in the iPhone app: the phone streams audio straight to an OpenAI realtime voice model, which answers in a natural voice and hands anything that needs tools or memory to the person's agent. It is one gateway-wide switch for iPhone Talk, not a per-person upgrade, so it is the later mode of VOX-01 and not a separate surface.
example: Hands full at the stove: Happy, how long do I rest a pork tenderloin... actually, first convert 425 Fahrenheit to a fan oven setting.
how:
`talk.realtime` block on the gateway: `provider` openai, a realtime model from the installed docs, `mode` realtime, `transport` webrtc (the iPhone path is client-owned WebRTC) and `brain` agent-consult so every tool call is routed through gateway policy on

-main. iOS client-owned WebRTC is Platform-key-only, so it needs an OpenAI Platform API key under `talk.realtime.providers.openai` (as a SecretRef), separate from the per-person chat provider ids. The host enforces a fresh spoken yes before high-impact actions started by voice. Finalized utterances are appended to the agent session so later text and voice turns share history.
depends_on: VOX-01 on Tony's phone, with the voice guardrails (VOX-03) in place
an OpenAI Platform key dedicated to voice
G004 spend caps extended to the voice key
decision: Zero Data Retention for the organisation that owns the voice key
caveats: Raw audio, not just text, goes to OpenAI for the whole call: with WebRTC the media runs directly between the device and the provider.

Billed separately from chat. OpenAI's pricing page lists gpt-live-1 at $0.05 per minute and gpt-realtime-mini at $10 in and $20 out per million audio tokens. Ten minutes a day on gpt-live-1 works out to about $15 a month per parent (my arithmetic). The price page says gpt-live-1 is billed per second and that backend model and tool usage are charged separately, so every agent-consult turn adds normal chat cost on top.
`talk.realtime` is one gateway-wide block, so the per-person provider ids and per-person cost split used for text do not carry over to voice.
The installed docs mark the iOS GPT-Live path as implemented with device live verification still pending, and GPT-Live sessions end at a 30-minute TTL.
In a kitchen with children talking in the background, their voices are streamed to a cloud model. Use it with the phone at the ear or headphones, or stay on VOX-01 push-to-talk.
For most kitchen questions the native loop is enough; realtime mainly buys barge-in and lower latency.

Retention: OpenAI's data-controls page lists the realtime endpoint with 30 days of abuse-monitoring retention unless the organisation has Zero Data Retention (the endpoint is eligible; GPT-Live sessions are listed separately and are also eligible). The M1 store-off decision covers chat calls through the custom provider ids and does not carry over to voice.
The spoken confirmation gates the action, not the speaker: anyone in earshot, a child included, can say yes. It applies to voice-originated consult runs only.
Usable only on a phone that is already paired, which today means the operator's phone (see VOX-01).

Turning on `talk.realtime` is one gateway-wide choice for iPhone Talk: the docs say OpenAI realtime configs run as WebRTC on iOS and only non-realtime configs use the native loop. It is not a per-person upgrade from VOX-01; a per-device opt-in is documented for the Mac app only.
The default and the limited pairing codes both hand the phone operator.talk.secrets, the scope for reading Talk configuration with secrets included.
safety:
`brain: agent-consult` keeps tools behind the same

-main policy, hooks and approvals as text. The spoken-confirmation gate is host-enforced, bound to the final arguments and consumed once, so generated text cannot confirm on the user's behalf; it does not identify who spoke. The realtime voice model is a second cloud model outside

-main's provider policy: it hears the room and is given a bounded slice of the session's history. Headphones or phone-at-ear is a habit, not a control, so this stays out of shared rooms when children are present. Never point realtime at a kids agent: it is cloud audio by construction.
unverified: Whether a store:false style retention control applies to realtime sessions.
Whether realtime credentials can be set per agent or per person.
Real latency and barge-in quality on the home Wi-Fi.
Whether this OpenAI organisation has Zero Data Retention; without it realtime audio falls under the 30-day abuse-monitoring window.
What the 'bounded realtime profile context' sent to the voice provider contains for an agent that holds personal memory.
Whether an iPhone can stay on the native loop while `talk.realtime` is configured.
Whether Talk configuration read with operator.talk.secrets includes the realtime provider key.

name: Home Assistant Voice Preview Edition kitchen speaker
description: The roadmap's kitchen speaker for the kids: a small open device with a physical microphone mute where wake word, speech-to-text and text-to-speech can all run locally in Home Assistant, so only text would be handed to Happy. It stays blocked until there is a local model and a kids agent, and the hop from Home Assistant to Happy still needs a small kids-only shim so the speaker never holds an operator credential.
example: Okay Nabu, what is the weather this afternoon?
how: Buy the device. Run Home Assistant OS in a VM on the Mac (documented minimum 2 GB RAM and 2 vCPUs; a VirtualBox image for Apple Silicon, or UTM). Add Whisper or Speech-to-Phrase for speech-to-text and Piper for speech through the Wyoming integration for a fully local pipeline. Then a conversation agent must forward the text to a stateless OpenClaw agent, and that hop is the unsolved part: Home Assistant's official OpenAI integration only talks to OpenAI's own endpoint, and OpenClaw's OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint (off by default; the config repo's flat config has it enabled on this gateway) is documented as full operator access. With token auth a bearer token gets the full operator scope set and the request's model field chooses the agent, so Home Assistant would hold an owner-level credential that can reach any agent unless a small kids-only shim sits in between, as the roadmap already notes.

Home Assistant OS VM on the Mac (the same VM HOM-01 would use)
a scoped endpoint or shim between Home Assistant and the gateway
kids agent (F072, M5)

It adds an always-on VM to patch and back up, in a house whose only Home Assistant relevant gear is Hue, Sonos and one TV.
Open-ended questions need Whisper, which Home Assistant recommends only on powerful hardware; the fast Speech-to-Phrase option covers home-control phrases only.

Without a local model, a speaker question reaches OpenAI as text. A room speaker cannot be made adults-only, because nothing identifies who is speaking, so there is no interim adult version: the device stays blocked until a local model exists.

Home Assistant's OpenAI page points to its OpenRouter integration for other providers and offers no custom base URL, so the bridge would be a community integration or a self-written shim (not verified which).

name: House devices by text: Hue lights and Sonos through a stateless home agent, with a read-only goodnight check
description: A parent texts Happy to switch Hue rooms and scenes by name, or to play a Sonos favourite, pause everything or set a room's volume, inside a room allowlist, a hard volume cap and quiet hours enforced in code. Separately, at 22:30 a parent gets a text only if lights or speakers are still on; that check switches nothing.
example: Jordan texts: 'Downstairs lights off and pause the music.' At 22:30, only if something is on: 'Still on: family room lights, living room Sonos.'
how: Step 1, read-only (F081): a command payload with no model runs openhue and sonos status on the Gateway host at 22:30 and prints `NO_REPLY` when everything is off; nothing is actuated. Step 2, switching: a sandboxed, stateless home agent reached by `sessions_spawn` holds two in-house plugins. Hue (F076) wraps the openhue CLI on the host, with the bridge key in ~/.openhue/config.yaml, a room allowlist and quiet hours in code. Sonos (F077) wraps the sonos CLI: favourites and allowlisted scenes only, a volume cap and a lower night cap in code; it needs the macOS Local Network permission for the gateway's node process, or `--ip` per speaker. Scheduled bedtime scenes are left to the Hue app, and the other bundled device skills stay uninstalled.
caveats: This switches things in the house, so the room allowlist, the volume caps and quiet hours are enforced in plugin code and not by the prompt.
Neither command-line tool is installed, and the bridge and the two speakers (living room and family room) come from the 9 Oct scan and were not re-checked.
Whether the launchd-run gateway needs the Local Network switch for plain HTTPS to the Hue bridge is unverified, since the bundled skills document it only for Sonos discovery.
The volume caps (35, and 10 at night) are design numbers and not sourced.
Play-by-search uses the music service already linked in the Sonos app, so Happy holds no music login, but auto-playing the first search hit has no content filter.
The Hue app can already switch lights at a set time and when you leave home, so Happy's part at night is the reminder and not the switching.
Whether the two tools report 'on' states in a form a short script can parse reliably has not been tried.
Home Assistant (HOM-01) is an alternative route to the same devices and not an addition, so pick one.
corrections: 'sonoscli is go install only' is wrong: the project's install page recommends Homebrew (a steipete tap) and also offers prebuilt release archives; go install needs Go 1.26 or later. Only the bundled skill's metadata is limited to go install, so Go does not have to be installed on the Mac mini.

'Isolated runs cannot approve' is too strong: the exec approvals doc says approvals from scheduled runs are delivered to connected approval clients (Control UI, the apps) and the run waits, but they never go to chat channels and are denied at once when no such client is connected. For an iMessage-only household the conclusion is unchanged: use a dry-run period, not per-call approval.

Whether the launchd-run gateway needs the Local Network switch for plain HTTPS to the bridge; the bundled skills document it only for Sonos discovery.
The bridge's presence on the LAN comes from the 9 Oct scan and was not re-checked (no LAN contact in this run).
The volume caps (35, and 10 at night) are design numbers, not sourced.

name: Sonos announce (intercom-style)
description: A parent texts an announcement and the house speakers say it, then go back to what they were playing. No route is both local and confirmed to resume the music without Home Assistant, so the first step is a choice between Home Assistant (HOM-01), the Sonos cloud API, or a plain play-uri that replaces what is playing.
example: Happy, tell the house the bus leaves in ten minutes.
how:
Trigger is deterministic, not a model decision: a `before_dispatch` claim on a fixed prefix such as `announce:` from an adult's handle hands the parent's words verbatim to the tool, so

-main (which reads search results) never decides to speak to the house and no cloud-written text is played to the children. If an agent tool form is kept, each announcement needs an approval. The tool itself, `announce(text, rooms)`, lives in the planned `home-sonos` plugin. It synthesizes the text with the local engine from VOX-04, serves the file from a small HTTP server bound to the LAN address only (one directory, short-lived random file names, inbound firewall exception for the speakers), and plays it. Route A, no Home Assistant: the Sonos audio-clip command `loadAudioClip` with a `streamUrl`, which mixes the clip with whatever is playing but is documented under the cloud Control API with OAuth and an API key; or sonoscli `play-uri`, which replaces what is playing and restores nothing. Route B, if Home Assistant is ever installed for VOX-11: its Sonos integration plays an announcement with `announce: true` and restores the volume. In code: text length cap, volume cap, quiet hours from G001, speaker allowlist, a daily cap.
depends_on: F077 Sonos plugin
VOX-04 local TTS
decision: Sonos account OAuth, Home Assistant, or local play-uri only
G001 notification policy
caveats: The bundled sonoscli skill documents discover, status, play, volume and grouping only; it has no announce or speech command. The tool's site lists `play-url` and `play-uri`, but I could not confirm that either resumes the previous music.
Sonos audio clips only work on players that report the AUDIO_CLIP capability; the two speakers here are unchecked.
LAN speaker control from the gateway needs the macOS Local Network permission for the launchd node process.
A talking house at the wrong moment is worse than no feature; quiet hours and a low daily cap matter more than voice quality.

The overlay is unverified without Home Assistant. Sonos documents loadAudioClip under its cloud Control API (OAuth scope plus API key), and Home Assistant's page says its announcements need TCP port 1443 open on each speaker, which suggests a local interface exists; Sonos' own page does not document one.
Home Assistant's page warns that older hardware and S1 firmware may not fully support announcements.
The 9 Oct scan found the two speakers in the living room and the family room, so an announcement does not reach the kitchen or bedrooms.
The Sonos cloud route puts a Sonos account token on the gateway and makes a house announcement depend on an internet round trip.

The speaker has to fetch the clip from the Mac over HTTP, so this adds a LAN-facing listener to a host whose gateway binds only to loopback today. It should serve nothing but the generated clip files and be covered by the host firewall review.
Sonos accepts only MP3 or WAV clips (the local engines emit WAV, which fits).

The `sonos` binary is not installed. The project's install page offers a Homebrew tap and prebuilt archives, so a Go toolchain is not needed; only the bundled skill's metadata is limited to `go install`.
safety:
The audience is everyone in the house, guests and children included, so this is an outbound channel in its own right even though nothing leaves the building. It must not be callable by an agent that reads untrusted content without an approval:

-main reads search and research results, so the safe trigger is a fixed prefix claimed before the model, speaking the parent's words verbatim. Never reachable from research or mail readers. Speech is synthesized locally, with the VOX-04 hardening in place. Text length, volume, quiet hours, speaker allowlist and a daily cap are enforced in code. No lock, alarm or door is involved.
unverified: Whether sonoscli `play-uri` restores the prior queue or stream after a clip.
Whether these two Sonos models support audio clips, and whether a purely local clip endpoint is usable without the Sonos cloud.
Latency from text to sound.
Whether the Sonos Control API route needs a registered developer integration (client id and secret) before OAuth works.

name: Home Assistant as the house hub, reached over MCP
description: One Home Assistant endpoint through which a stateless home agent reads state and controls only the entities a parent has exposed, covering Hue, Sonos and the LG TV with one audited list instead of one plugin per brand. It is an alternative to the direct Hue and Sonos plugins (F076, F077), not an addition: pick one path. It needs a Home Assistant VM on the Mac mini, which the roadmap already plans for the kids' speaker (VOX-11). OpenClaw 2026.9.7 has no Home Assistant, HomeKit, Matter or MQTT integration of its own; Home Assistant's MCP Server integration is the official route.
example: Are any lights or the TV still on downstairs?
how: Run Home Assistant OS in a VM on the Mac mini (the roadmap already plans this VM for the kids' speaker). Add the Hue, Sonos and LG webOS integrations, then the 'Model Context Protocol Server' integration; turn off 'Expose all LLM APIs' and expose only the wanted entities. In OpenClaw add mcp.servers.<name> with url http://<ha-host>:8123/api/mcp, transport 'streamable-http' written out (when it is omitted OpenClaw uses sse), and the Home Assistant long-lived token in headers.Authorization, supplied through a secret reference and not a config literal (auth 'oauth' with openclaw mcp login is the documented alternative). This Gateway uses tools.profile 'minimal', which hides MCP tools, so grant them only to the stateless 'home' agent from F076 by listing the <server>__<tool> names in that agent's alsoAllow and in its sandbox tool allow list (tools.sandbox.tools.alsoAllow); no other agent then sees the server. Write toolFilter.include after a live probe (openclaw mcp doctor <name> --probe), since it selects tools by name. The registry before_tool_call hook stays as the second, fail-closed gate and enforces quiet hours.
depends_on: Home Assistant OS VM (2 GB RAM, 2 vCPU, bridged network adapter)
stateless home agent (F076)
egress proxy exception for the Home Assistant LAN address
decision: direct CLIs (F076/F077) or Home Assistant as the single device path, not both
caveats: The MCP server does not support notifications or sampling, so Home Assistant cannot push a state change to Happy through MCP; Happy can only ask.
A HomeKit accessory can pair with only one controller, so the LG TV stays in Apple Home and joins Home Assistant through the webOS integration, not through HomeKit.
Running both the direct CLIs and Home Assistant doubles the paths to the same lamp; pick one.
With only Hue, two Sonos speakers and one TV today, the hub pays off mainly if announcements (VOX-07) or the kids' speaker (VOX-11) are also wanted.

Home Assistant's macOS page documents VirtualBox (UTM only as a fallback for people used to virtual machines) and points anyone not comfortable with virtual machines to a dedicated board; the VM is one more service to patch, back up and bring back after every reboot and FileVault unlock, and until it is up every home tool fails.

Home Assistant's MCP server offers its Assist intents plus any scripts exposed to Assist, not arbitrary actions; anything beyond on/off, brightness, volume and state reads (announcements, TV notices) needs a script a parent writes and exposes.

Because those tools are generic intents, toolFilter.include narrows verbs, not device classes; the exposure list in Home Assistant and a before_tool_call check on each call's target are the real limits.

The long-lived token is a ten-year credential for Home Assistant's APIs as one user; the exposed-entity limit applies to the MCP tools, not to the token, so it must stay host-side and be rotated by hand.
State text returned by Home Assistant (now-playing titles, device names) is third-party text read by an agent that can actuate; allowlists and caps in code have to bound the result.

Home Assistant's MCP options 'Expose all LLM APIs' and 'Require an administrator account' are both on by default: out of the box every LLM API is offered and the token must belong to an administrator. Tighten the first before OpenClaw connects; a token for a non-admin Home Assistant user works only after the second is turned off.
Home Assistant exposes new entities in the cover domain (garage doors and gates) to Assist by default, so the exposure list needs a review after each device is added.
safety: The home agent keeps no memory, has no web tool and no outbound message tool, so it holds no private data and cannot send anything out; the only outside text it reads is device state. Only exposed entities are reachable through MCP; locks, garage, alarm, gate and cameras are never exposed in Home Assistant, and a fail-closed hook that inspects each call's target repeats that block on the OpenClaw side. The token is a wider credential than the MCP tools and is kept host-side only.
unverified: Whether Home Assistant OS runs cleanly under VirtualBox or UTM on macOS 27 with an M5 chip.
Whether openclaw mcp login completes against Home Assistant's OAuth; both sides document OAuth but the pair was not tried, so the long-lived token path is assumed.
The exact tool names Home Assistant's MCP server exposes (not listed on the page fetched), so the toolFilter list must be written after a live probe.
Whether the Smokescreen egress proxy applies to MCP HTTP calls to a LAN address.
Whether a non-administrator Home Assistant user can use the MCP endpoint once 'Require an administrator account' is turned off, and what that user can still reach.
Whether a Home Assistant long-lived token is confined to the MCP endpoint or carries its owner's full API rights; the authentication page fetched does not say.
Which macOS account runs the VM and how it comes back headless after a reboot (FileVault needs a manual unlock).

name: Multi-day family project with check-ins
description: A parent hands Happy a project with an end date (birthday party, weekend trip, garage clean-out). Happy keeps one project note with decisions and open items, checks in on a schedule it paces itself, runs research legs in the background, and stops when the date passes. The one-shot plan in F028 keeps no state and sends no check-ins.
example: Plan our 10-year-old's birthday party for Saturday the 14th: 10 kids, indoor, under 300 dollars. Check in with me every few days until it is sorted.
how:
Held by the asking parent's

-main. State: one project note (memory/projects/.md through the F041 write path, or home-store rows from F031) with goal, end date, decisions, open items and a review date. The note records only what the parent typed or confirmed, written in a turn that carried no web or research results. Check-ins: one isolated automation per project, created through the `automations` tool on

-main with a `pacing` object (`min`, `max`; `--pacing-min` and `--pacing-max` are the CLI spelling), so each run can call `automations(action: "next_check")` and be clamped to those bounds. The job's tool cap holds the note or home-store read tools plus `automations` (inside an automation run that tool is limited to the run's own job) and never `sessions_spawn` or a web tool; announce to the owner; NO_REPLY when nothing is due; the run removes its own job after the end date. Hard prerequisites before `automations` is allowed on

-main: the fail-closed before_tool_call pin must also match `automations`/`cron` add and update and refuse webhook delivery, completion and failure destinations, and any recipient other than the asking parent; and `cron.triggers.enabled: false`, so the tool does not offer script payloads, trigger scripts or stream commands. Research legs: `sessions_spawn` to the stateless `research` agent with `runTimeoutSeconds` and `completionTarget: "parent"`, in interactive turns only, so

-main reviews the result privately before it texts anything. Decisions are plain proposals in chat (or `ask_user` while the parent is in the conversation). `/goal` is not the durable state here: the 04:00 reset wipes it.
depends_on: F041 memory write path or F031 home-store

F007 automations tool on

-main
F019 research agent
G009 delivery pin, extended to cover automations/cron add and update and to refuse webhook delivery
G001 notification policy
decision: Jordan as a command owner
cron.triggers.enabled: false (AUT-08)
caveats: Scheduled runs do not get MEMORY.md injected, so a check-in must read the project note with a tool or carry the state in the job message.
A job created from chat is capped to the tools the creating turn had and cannot be widened later, so a check-in can never do more than the parent's own main agent.
The conversation resets every morning at 04:00 and that also wipes any /goal; the project note is the only continuity between days.
Every check-in is a cloud model turn. Pace in days, not minutes, and cap active projects per person (three is plenty).
No bookings, purchases or invitations sent: the output is options, links and drafts. A static checklist is still easier in a shared Notes or Reminders list; Happy adds the nudging and the research.

The one long-task measurement opened in this run dates from March 2025 and covers software tasks: the frontier model of that time finished about half of the tasks that take a person roughly 50 minutes. It says nothing direct about gpt-6-sol or about family planning. The case for many short runs with a parent between them rests on cost and on keeping a person in the loop, not on that number.

Command-owner status is gateway-wide: an owner can ask their agent to list, inspect, update, run or remove any job on the gateway, whoever created it. Once Jordan is an owner, each parent's agent can read and change the other's check-in jobs, so job messages must not carry private detail.

The F041 plan refuses memory writes in a turn tainted by web results, and a turn that received a research result is tainted. Research findings therefore cannot be saved into the project note in that turn: they stay in the chat thread, and the note holds only what the parent states or confirms afterwards.

OpenClaw's own guidance is to deny the scheduling tool by default on any agent that handles untrusted content (docs/gateway/security/tool-permissions.md).

-main reads search snippets, so granting it `automations` is a deliberate exception that rests on the delivery pin and on triggers staying off.
safety:
-main holds the note and never browses; `research` does every web leg, has no memory, and as a sub-agent can never get the message, cron or gateway tools. The `automations` tool is itself a send path: a job can name any chat as its delivery target or post its result to a webhook URL.

-main holds memory and reads search snippets, so the recipient pin must cover `automations`/`cron` calls, not only `message`, and must refuse webhook mode before the tool is granted. Check-in runs carry no web tool and no `sessions_spawn`; that is the hard limit. The rule that handoff text carries dates, ages and budget only (never names, school or address) is prompt text, not enforcement. With the pin in place nothing on the never list is reachable: there is no payment, booking or outbound-to-strangers tool anywhere in the chain.
unverified: Whether a custom-session job (`--session session:<id>`) is exempt from the daily reset policy, which would let check-ins keep conversational context.
Whether memory read tools can be named in a job tool cap for a sandboxed agent on 2026.9.7; test at build time.
That research handoffs return results with agent-to-agent off and session visibility self (already an open item in the roadmap).
Whether the gateway accepts webhook delivery or an arbitrary recipient on a job that an agent creates from an iMessage owner turn. The tool description offers both; it was not tested.
Whether next_check and self-removal stay callable when the job's tool cap leaves out `automations`.
Whether the F041 path hook, written for memory/*.md, admits a memory/projects/ subfolder.

adds: From AUT-03 (Self-paced watch loop (/loop and paced automations)): The /loop command runs on the same scheduling tool and needs the same prerequisites as AUT-01's check-ins: the delivery pin extended to automations add and update with webhooks refused, cron.triggers.enabled false, and owner status. If that grant is ever made, /loop works for an owner too; house rule is an explicit interval of 15 minutes or more and a stop condition, and since it sees only search snippets, page watching stays with F029. The round-1 review of OCL-06 takes /loop out of that entry, so this note is where /loop is described.
review_notes: All nine sources check out, but the safety case has a hole: the `automations` tool this feature depends on can set a job's delivery to any chat or to a webhook URL, and command-owner status lets either parent's agent read and edit the other's jobs. The project note also collides with the F041 rule that tainted turns cannot write memory. Value lowered to 3.
